transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I’m here because my sleep has basically fallen apart. I'll just lie in bed in my apartment for hours. My laptop will be closed, but I'm still mentally rechecking work deadlines, tuition payments, class assignments... my brain just keeps going. And even when I finally do manage to sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really turned off.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things, even when there's no apparent reason to worry?

Yeah, definitely. My mind just keeps jumping around. I'll start worrying about whether I'm falling behind at work, and then it shifts to whether I'm wasting money on school, or... or if my family is going to think I can't handle things. It's just constant. I basically treat every small issue like it could completely derail my whole future, even when nothing is actually wrong.
Has something very stressful or traumatic happened to you recently?
No, not really. I mean, there hasn't been any big event or trauma or anything like that. Just the usual stuff... work, school, paying bills. But nothing out of the ordinary has happened.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain activities or places because of your worries?

No, I don't think so. I still go to work, I still go to class... I mean, I might be stressed the whole time I'm there, but I don't really avoid going to places or doing things. I just worry while I'm doing them.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of sadness or hopelessness lately?

No, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless. It's more just... I'm always wound up and stressed about everything. But I don't feel down in that way, just really overwhelmed by all the constant worrying.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or stomach problems?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I don't get headaches, and my stomach has been fine. So... no, no physical issues like pain or being sick. It's really just the constant worrying.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worrying?

It's been going on for about a year and three months now. It started right around the time I began an evening graduate certificate program... I kept my full-time job as an analyst, so doing both at the same time is really when all this constant worrying began.
Have you ever experienced or witnessed something traumatic that you try not to think about?

No, I haven't. Um, nothing like that. I haven't been through any kind of trauma or major accidents, and there's nothing from my past that I'm trying to block out. It's really just the everyday stress from work and school that I can't seem to stop worrying about.
Do you find yourself avoiding thoughts or memories of any specific past event?

No, um... not at all. Like I was just saying, there isn't really any specific event from my past that I'm trying to avoid. I don't have any bad memories I'm running from or anything. It's really just... just the current stuff with my job and my classes that I can't seem to stop stressing over.
Do you ever experience sudden, intense episodes of fear or discomfort that reach a peak within minutes?

No, not really. It doesn't really hit me all at once like that. It's more just... a constant, exhausting worry that's always there in the background, all day long. But I don't get those sudden spikes of intense fear you're talking about.
Has your constant worrying been interfering with your ability to function at work or in your personal relationships?

Yeah, it really has. Um, I’ve actually started missing work deadlines lately, which is hard to admit. And I’m falling behind in my certificate classes, too. It just takes up so much of my mental energy. Outside of work... I've pretty much stopped doing all the normal routines that used to keep me grounded. Like, I don't do yoga or go running anymore, and I've completely stopped cooking. It's just getting in the way of everything right now.
Have you noticed that your worrying tends to focus on a specific set of concerns, such as work or school, or does it seem more free-floating and unpredictable?

Um, it definitely jumps around a lot. It's not just one single thing. My mind just keeps jumping from whether I’m falling behind at work, to... whether I’m wasting money on school. And then I start worrying about whether my family will think I can’t handle things. It just builds on itself. I basically treat every small issue like it could completely derail my whole future.
Are you finding it difficult to enjoy time with friends or family because of your worrying?

Um, I'm not really sure about that. I haven't really noticed it being an issue, to be honest. I mean, I worry about what my family thinks of me, like I mentioned, but... I don't know if the worrying actually stops me from enjoying the time I spend with them. I just haven't really paid attention to that specifically.
Do you find yourself trying to avoid thoughts, feelings, or conversations related to any past events?

No, not really. I mean, my worries are mostly about what's happening right now or what's going to happen in the future. I don't really find myself avoiding things from the past. It's more just... the everyday stuff that keeps me on edge.
Do you usually start worrying when something specific happens or when you're in a particular situation?

Not really. I mean, there isn't usually a specific event or situation that sets it off. It just kind of... starts on its own. Honestly, it feels like it's just always running in the background, no matter where I am or what I'm doing. It doesn't really take a specific trigger to get me going.
Does your worrying affect most areas of your life, such as work, school, and personal relationships, or is it mostly focused on one or two specific areas?

Um, I'd say it affects pretty much all areas. It's definitely not just focused on one or two things. 

My mind just keeps jumping around... like, from whether I'm falling behind at work, to whether I'm wasting money on school, to whether my family will think I just can't handle things. It doesn't stay in one lane. I basically end up treating every small issue like it could completely derail my whole future. So, yeah, it really touches everything.
Would you say that your worrying is causing you a lot of distress?

Yes, absolutely. It's... it's causing a lot of problems for me. I've actually started missing work deadlines recently, and I'm falling behind in my certificate classes. And I've just... I've stopped doing all the routines that used to keep me grounded. Like, I haven't been doing yoga or running, and I don't even really cook anymore. The worry just kind of takes over all my time and energy.
Do you think you've had a single day in the past year where you didn't worry about something?

No, I really don't think I have. Actually, this has been going on for about a year and three months now. It... it all started right around the time I began an evening graduate certificate program, while still keeping my full-time job as an analyst. So, yeah, it's been pretty much every single day since then.
